frequency_question: How often do structural friction and intervention mechanisms successfully prevent or delay executive-ordered major tariffs past their target implementation date?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly threatened or formally signed broad sweeping or sectoral tariffs by U.S. presidents where domestic legal challenge, legislative pushback, or structural institutional friction was actively mobilized; excludes routine anti-dumping administrative duties.

cases.name: 2019 Proposed Tariffs on All Mexican Goods

coverage_note: 5 major instances identified matching executive tariff threats involving key trading partners facing structural/institutional friction.
known_gaps: Excludes minor narrow-product exclusions granted through administrative petition processes, focusing only on macro-level threats.
validity_reason: Relies on executive authority frameworks under current trade laws (Trade Expansion Act of 1962, Trade Act of 1974) which remain stable across administrations until legislative reform occurs.
